newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index drops further as crown fears.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index drops further as crown fears.

text.p: Slovak shares were quiet in listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, as foreign investors, fearing a weakening of the crown, take a wait-and-see attitude.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta fell 80 crowns to 1,320 -- though only five shares traded -- as the SAX index slipped 0.7 points to 176.94.

Foreign investors, who traders say are the only players who can increase market liquidity and more significantly move shares in either direction, have virtually stopped all their activities on the Slovak capital market.
"They (foreigners) all think the crown is overvalued and that some depreciation must come in the foresseable future," said one local stock trader.
Brokers said low liquidity and a downtrend were expected to continue to plague the BSE in coming weeks. Only 311 shares were traded on the main BSE listed market on Friday.

Overall volume decreased to 223,231 shares, from 229,298 stocks traded on Thursday. Turnover fell to 105.25 million crowns, from 185.69 million crowns on Thursday. -- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402
